detail.unreachableBody: Their repository is offline. The backups still exist and aren’t lost — they can’t be restored or deleted until the repository comes back online.

hostDetail.removeKeptRest: You can still restore from them, and re-registering the server later picks them back up.

point.offlineTip: This restore point’s repository is offline — it can’t be read until the repository comes back online.
point.blockedCorrupt: This restore point failed its backup-file health check and is blocked from restore.
point.blockedWriteFailed: The backup files could not be written completely, so this point can't be restored.
point.blockedWritePending: Backup files are still being written. Wait for the restore point to complete.
point.blockedHealthCheck: A health check is currently reading this restore point. Wait for it to finish before restoring.
point.encryptedTip: This backup's data is encrypted at rest
point.fileWriteFailedTip: The restore-point files were not written completely.
point.sizeFullTitle: Complete logical recovery image captured by this restore point, before data reduction
point.sizeIncrTitle: Logical change data captured by this restore point, before data reduction
point.noNewDataTip: No new repository data was reported for this point. It can still be fully restorable through chunks already stored by earlier backups.
point.newDataTip: New data this restore point added to the repository after deduplication and compression. This is not the restore point’s total physical footprint.
point.deleteTip: Delete this full backup and its incremental restore points

health.corruptTip: This restore point failed its backup-file health check and is blocked from restore.
health.unavailableTip: The backup-file health check could not read this restore point.

calendar.noPointDay: No restore point on this day
calendar.noPointsDay: No restore points were created on this day. Pick a highlighted day to see its points.

deleteOne.deletedDesc_one: The backup for {{name}} was removed. Its storage is reclaimed on the next cleanup.
deleteOne.deletedDesc_other: The backup for {{name}} — {{count}} restore points — was removed. Its storage is reclaimed on the next cleanup.
deleteOne.errorDesc: The backup could not be removed. Try again in a moment.
deleteOne.title: Delete this backup?
deleteOne.desc: This permanently removes every restore point in this backup — full and incremental together. It can't be undone. There is no way to delete a single point on its own.
deleteOne.recoverWarn: Once removed, you won't be able to recover <1>{{name}}</1> to any point in this backup.
deleteOne.gfsTitle: This backup is kept by a GFS policy
deleteOne.gfsWarn_one: {{count}} restore point in this backup is marked for long-term retention (grandfather-father-son). Deleting it discards an archive copy the policy was holding.
deleteOne.gfsWarn_other: {{count}} restore points in this backup are marked for long-term retention (grandfather-father-son). Deleting them discards archive copies the policy was holding.
deleteOne.gfsWarnUnknown: This backup holds restore points marked for long-term retention (grandfather-father-son). Deleting it discards archive copies the policy was holding.

addPhysical.registeredDesc: The agent is inventorying its disks and volumes. Add it to a backup job to start protecting it.
addPhysical.errorDesc: The appliance couldn't reach that address or deploy the agent. Check the name and IP, then try again.
addPhysical.title: Register a physical server
addPhysical.description: AltaStor deploys its backup agent to the server and inventories its disks and volumes. Back it up bare-metal, per disk, or file-level — same as a VM, no hypervisor needed.
addPhysical.osHint: Picks the enrollment path — the agent reports the exact OS once it’s up.
addPhysical.note: The server stays unprotected until a backup job includes it. Removing it later keeps its restore points.

sourceSettings.description: Rescan its inventory, remove it, or update its agent.

removeEnvironment.title: Remove {{name}}?
removeEnvironment.description: Stops discovery and removes <1>{{hosts}} hosts and {{vms}} VMs</1> from Inventory. Existing restore points are kept and stay restorable.
removeEnvironment.jobsBlock_one: <1>{{count}}</1> job still targets this environment — repoint or remove it first.
removeEnvironment.jobsBlock_other: <1>{{count}}</1> jobs still target this environment — repoint or remove them first.
removeEnvironment.jobsWarning_one: <1>{{count}}</1> job currently targets this environment. It will fail on the next run until re-pointed at another environment.
removeEnvironment.jobsWarning_other: <1>{{count}}</1> jobs currently target this environment. They will fail on the next run until re-pointed at another environment.

failed.description: The environment could not be removed. Try again in a moment.

addEnvironment.title: Add environment
addEnvironment.description: Register a VMware vCenter Server, a standalone ESXi host, or a Hyper-V host or cluster so AltaStor can discover and protect its VMs.

vcenter.label: VMware vCenter
vcenter.hint: vCenter Server managing one or more ESXi hosts.

esxiStandalone.label: VMware ESXi (standalone)
esxiStandalone.hint: A single ESXi host, managed directly.

hyperv.label: Microsoft Hyper-V
hyperv.hint: A Hyper-V host, or any node or the name of a failover cluster. AltaStor needs WinRM (5986 or 5985) and SMB (445) to every node, and an account that is a local administrator on each.

addEnvironment.addressInvalid: Enter a valid FQDN or IP address — no protocol, path, or spaces.

editEnvironment.passwordPlaceholder: Leave blank to keep the current password

rescan.failedDesc_one: The appliance couldn’t reach {{count}} environment, so nothing was refreshed.
rescan.failedDesc_other: The appliance couldn’t reach {{count}} environments, so nothing was refreshed.
rescan.partialDesc: {{ok}} of {{total}} environments were refreshed; the appliance couldn’t reach the rest.
rescan.oneFailedDesc: The appliance couldn’t reach it, so its inventory is unchanged.

syntheticFull.actionTip: Merge this VM's backup chain into a new full restore point, without reading the VM
syntheticFull.title: Create a synthetic full
syntheticFull.desc: Merge {{vm}}'s stored backup chain into a new full restore point. The merge happens inside the repository — nothing is read from the VM or sent over the network.
syntheticFull.descRunning: Merging {{vm}}'s backup chain into a new full restore point.
syntheticFull.resultNote: Result: one new full restore point. The points above are kept and stay restorable.
syntheticFull.targetSameHint: The merged full is written alongside the chain it came from.
syntheticFull.targetOtherHint: The chain is read from its own repository and the merged full is written to this one.

inherited.title: The merged full will use
inherited.note: These come from the job and the target repository, not from this run — change them in <1>{{job}}</1> and they apply to every run, including this one.

syntheticFull.jobScopeNote_one: The appliance runs a synthetic full per job, so {{job}} will also merge the chain of {{count}} other VM it protects.
syntheticFull.jobScopeNote_other: The appliance runs a synthetic full per job, so {{job}} will also merge the chains of {{count}} other VMs it protects.
syntheticFull.sourceDegraded: {{repository}} is reporting problems. The merge reads every point in the chain, so it may take longer than usual or fail partway.

progress.doneNote: The new full restore point is in the list, and the incrementals that follow will chain onto it.

toast.startedDesc: Merging {{vm}}'s backup chain. It appears in Activity like any other run.

syntheticFull.badgeTip: A full restore point built by merging the chain in the repository, rather than by reading the VM

refusal.no-job: No backup job has produced restore points for this VM yet, so there is no chain to merge.
refusal.no-chain: This job hasn't produced any restore points for this VM yet, so there is no chain to merge.
refusal.chain-not-anchored: This chain's oldest restore point is an incremental, with no full backup beneath it. A synthetic full needs a full backup to merge onto.
refusal.no-incrementals: The chain holds only a full backup with no incrementals, so a synthetic full would copy it unchanged.
refusal.source-repository-unsupported: {{repository}} can't merge a backup chain. Synthetic fulls need a local or object-storage repository.
refusal.source-repository-offline: {{repository}} is unreachable, so the chain stored in it can't be read.
refusal.target-repository-unsupported: {{repository}} can't hold a merged backup. Pick a local or object-storage repository.
refusal.target-repository-offline: {{repository}} is unreachable, so the merged full can't be written to it.
refusal.job-running: {{job}} is running. Wait for it to finish — a merge started now would read a chain that is still being written to.

failure.generic: The merge failed. The run's log has the appliance's account of it.
failure.mismatchedDisks: The restore points in this chain describe different disks — a disk was added to or removed from the VM partway through it. Run a full backup to start a new chain, then merge that.
failure.missingArtifacts: Some restore points in this chain no longer have their stored backup files, so the chain can't be merged. Verify the repository, then run a full backup to start a fresh chain.
failure.outOfSpace: The target repository ran out of space. A synthetic full needs room for a whole new full backup before the old points age out.
failure.permissionDenied: The appliance couldn't write to the target repository. Check the repository's credentials and the permissions on its storage.
failure.repositoryGone: A repository this merge needed is no longer registered on the appliance.
failure.destinationCollision: The merged full would be written exactly where the chain it reads from is stored. Pick a different target repository.
failure.repositoryUnsupported: The repository can't merge a backup chain. Synthetic fulls need a local or object-storage repository.
failure.invalidChain: The chain isn't in a state that can be merged: it has to start with a full backup and hold only incrementals after it.
failure.noIncrementals: The chain holds only a full backup with no incrementals, so a synthetic full would copy it unchanged.

hypervConfig.title: Hyper-V configuration
hypervConfig.checkpointsNote_one: This VM has {{count}} checkpoint. Backups work as usual, but recovery to the original location is refused until it is deleted: replacing the disks would break the checkpoint chain. Restore to a new location instead, or delete the checkpoint first.
hypervConfig.checkpointsNote_other: This VM has {{count}} checkpoints. Backups work as usual, but recovery to the original location is refused until they are deleted: replacing the disks would break the checkpoint chain. Restore to a new location instead, or delete the checkpoints first.
